title: Partition (assay2chip stage S4)
description: The multi-chip plan: which unit ops go on which chip, what carries between the chips, and where the assay was cut. One assay does not fit on one chip - port count, area, incompatible temperatures and cross-contamination force a split - so this file is the heart of the pipeline. Written to assay2chip/work/<id>/partition.json. Every hand-off says whether a machine can do it (`automated`); the count of false ones is the headline number in the S10 report, because 'no human intervention' is the stated goal. Shape defined in assay2chip/README.md.

id.description: The run id, same as the work directory name and as unitops.json.

placeholder.description: true while this plan is made up rather than derived from real ops.

extraction.description: Carried forward from assay.json, so the plan still says which extractor produced the steps underneath it.

audit.description: S4's own working: what was tried, which constraint bound first, how the cuts were chosen.

chips.description: One entry per chip, in process order. Every op in unitops.json whose placement is on_chip must appear on exactly one chip.

chip_id.description: Becomes chip/designs/<chip_id>.json and then chip/<chip_id>.json, so it must be a legal id: lowercase, digits, underscores.

ops.description: The unitops.json `op` numbers this chip performs, in process order.

scale.description: Which envelope the chip is built to: demo is 30 x 20 mm (what can be printed today), target is the ANSI/SLAS microplate footprint 127.76 x 85.48 mm. Both from contracts/blocks.json through assay2chip/lib/contracts.envelope(); 290 x 190 mm is the ceiling, not a design scale.

reason.description: Why these ops are together on one chip, in one sentence.

area_mm2.description: Estimated area the ops need, when known, for comparison against the envelope.

ports.description: Ports this chip needs. The demo limit is fabrication_floors.max_ports_per_chip (6) and it is the usual reason a split is forced; read it from contracts, never as a literal.

temp_range_c.description: [min, max] temperature on this chip, when known. Two ops that cannot share a thermal zone cannot share a chip.

audit.description: Why this chip ended up with these ops: the area, port and temperature sums behind the decision.

handoffs.description: What moves between two chips, and how. Every boundary between consecutive chips needs one.

from_port.description: Outlet port id on that chip, e.g. outlet_1.

to_port.description: Inlet port id on that chip, e.g. inlet_1.

carries.description: What travels. It sets the line diameter, the settling risk and whether dead volume loses the sample.

volume_ul.description: Microlitres transferred. null when not yet known - and then it belongs in `unresolved`.

particle_um.description: Diameter of the largest thing in the line (swollen capsules, not unswollen), so the tubing and both ports can be checked against it.

automated.description: REQUIRED. true only if a machine can do this hand-off unattended (tubing, a selector valve, a syringe pump). Manual pipetting, a centrifuge spin or carrying a plate across the bench is false. The S10 report counts the false ones, and that count is the honest answer to 'does this run without a human?' - so never set it true to make the number look better.

how.description: The mechanism, in a few words: 'tubing + selector valve', 'manual pipette, 40 uL'. Required so `automated` can be checked by a reader.

risks.description: What can go wrong in the line: dead volume, sedimentation, shear at the connector, bubbles.

dead_volume_ul.description: Volume left in the line, when known; S9 checks it against volume_ul.

audit.description: The grounds for `automated`: what machine does it, or what a human has to do.

cuts.description: REQUIRED, may be empty: where the op sequence was cut and why. One entry per boundary, so the reasoning behind the split is reviewable rather than implicit in the chip list.

between.description: The two consecutive op numbers the cut falls between, e.g. [3, 4].

why.description: The constraint that forced the cut, in one sentence: port count, area, temperature, cross-contamination.

forced_by.description: Which of the hard constraints did it, for the report's tally.

unresolved.description: REQUIRED, may be empty. Carried forward from unitops.json and added to: anything this plan needed and nobody has stated, especially hand-off volumes and whether a hand-off can really be automated.

assumed.description: The value used instead, if any.

assumed_from.description: The contract key it came from. Never a bare literal.

audit.description: A deliberately OPEN object for the writing stage's working: every other field here is closed, but provenance must never be blocked by a schema. Nothing downstream may depend on its shape.

llm.description: Which language-model mode produced this file (assay2chip/lib/llm.py fills it in).

mode.description: stub means the deterministic offline fallback ran: treat every number as made up.
